# dsh-cite-verify
**Verify that a citation exists — and that its metadata is right.**
*DOI / PMID / arXiv / BibTeX → the provider's own answer, field-by-field checks, a content-addressed
snapshot, and a REP evidence record. `not_found` is reported as skipped, never as fabrication.*
English · 简体中文
## What it does
- Resolves `doi` through **Crossref**, `pmid` through **PubMed E-utilities**, `arxiv` through the **

arXiv Atom API**.
- Compares the citation as written against the resolved record: **title** (token s

imilarity), **authors** (family names), **year** (±1 = warning), **venue**, **pages**.
- Stores the
provider's exact response as an immutable snapshot and registers a **REP v1 evidence item** with tho

se checks.
- `cite_fix` returns a corrected BibTeX entry **as text** — it never edits files.
## What it does not do
- **No title search.** You must supply an identifier (DOI/PMID/arXiv/BibTeX). "Find me a paper that

says X" is a different plugin.
- **No retraction monitoring.** v0.1 only reports update notices atta
ched to the resolved record itself (`update-to`); deciding whether a work is retracted needs `dsh-re

traction-watch` (W2).
- **No PDF reading.** That is `dsh-doc-anchor`.
- **No scraping.** Only the fo

ur allowlisted HTTPS APIs; no CNKI, no Sci-Hub, no paywall bypass.
- **No silent repair.** `cite_fix
` reports diffs; applying them is the user's decision.

## Tools
### `cite_verify`
| Parameter | Type | Notes |

| `doi` / `pmid` / `arxiv` | string | at least one identifier (or `bibtex`) |
| `bibtex` | string |

entry supplies the identifier **and** the expected fields |
| `title`, `authors`, `year`, `venue`, `

pages` | | fields as cited, compared against the record |
| `fresh` | boolean | bypass the response

Returns `{ ok, status, notFound, lookupError, resolved, checks[], evidenceId, recordPath?, warnings[
ns `{ ok, status, notFound, lookupError, resolved, checks[], evidenceId, recordPath?, warnings[] }`.
`notFound` is true **only** when no provider returned a record, at least one definitively returned 4
04, and no lookup failed. `lookupError` is true when a network failure, timeout, 5xx or unparsable r
esponse prevented a check — that answer is `unchecked` and must not be read as “no record found”. If
one identifier fails while another resolves, the record is still returned with `lookupError: true`.
`status` is derived from the checks: any `fail` → `fail`, any `warn` → `warn`, any `pass` → `ok`, no
thing checked → `unchecked`.
### `cite_batch`
`{ citations: string[], fresh? }` where each item is `doi:10...`, `pmid:123`, `arxiv:2401.00001`, an
`@article{...}` entry, or a bare identifier detected by shape. Bounded concurrency, per-item failur
es, duplicate detection.
Each item carries `status`, `lookupError?`, `duplicate?` and `evidenceId?`. A repeated identifier is
marked `duplicate: true`; it keeps `fail` if it already failed (a duplicate never downgrades the wo
rst status) and is otherwise raised to `warn`. The batch `warnings[]` counts the duplicates.
### `cite_fix`
Same inputs as `cite_verify`. Returns `{ ok, bibtex, diffs[], status, evidenceId?, warnings[] }`. **
Text only — never writes to disk.**
### Error codes
`INVALID_INPUT` · `INVALID_BIBTEX` · `UNSUPPORTED_IDENTIFIER` · `STORE_ERROR` · `BATCH_TOO_LARGE`
Network failures never become citation failures: they appear as `skipped` checks (`network_error`, `
rate_limited`, `unavailable` for timeouts), set `lookupError: true`, and leave the evidence `uncheck
ed` with `notFound: false`.
## Check semantics
| Check | pass | fail / warn | skipped |

| `doi-exists` | Crossref returned the DOI | — | `not_found` when Crossref has no such DOI |
| `othe

r` (PMID/arXiv existence) | provider returned the record | — | `not_found` |
| `metadata-match` (tit

le) | similarity ≥ `titleThreshold` | `fail` below threshold | — |
| `metadata-match` (authors) | al

l cited family names present | `warn` ≥50 %, else `fail` | — |
| `metadata-match` (year) | exact | `

warn` ±1, `fail` otherwise | — |
| `metadata-match` (venue) | similarity ≥ 0.6 | `warn` | — |
| `met

adata-match` (pages) | normalized equality | `warn` | — |
| `version-match` | two identifiers agree

on the title | `warn` on disagreement | — |

## Security boundaries

- Documents are not read; only JSON/XML metadata from four allowlisted hosts.
- Response bodies beco

me immutable snapshots; the evidence records the **URL** and the provider, never credentials.
- Redi

rect and allowlist checks prevent SSRF through an allowed host.
- No telemetry, no tokens, no upload
s of user data (the query goes to the public metadata API, as it must).
## Known limitations (v0.1)
- **Retraction status is not queried.** Only the resolved record's own `update-to` notices are surfa

ced, with a warning. True monitoring is `dsh-retraction-watch`.
- **Crossref-only metadata for DOIs.

** OpenAlex is allowlisted but not yet used as a second opinion.
- **Author comparison is family-nam
e based.** Name particles and transliterations can differ; a mismatch is a warning, not proof of a w

rong citation.
- **BibTeX parsing is a subset** (no macro expansion, nested braces preserved verbati

m).
- **Cache can be stale** up to `cacheTtlMs`; use `fresh` when it matters.
